symbols.name: \(\epsilon\)
symbols.def: Fixed lower bound on both treatment probabilities.

symbols.name: \(M\)
symbols.def: Fixed known scale used for the conditional-mean interval and conditional fourth central moment.

symbols.name: \(\sigma\)
symbols.def: Fixed known radius for cellwise deviations from the average treatment effect, measured in units of \(M\).

symbols.name: \(c_{\epsilon}\)
symbols.def: A positive constant depending only on \(\epsilon\).

symbols.name: \(C_{\epsilon}\)
symbols.def: A finite constant depending only on \(\epsilon\).

symbols.name: \(j\)
symbols.def: Second generic observed-unit index, distinct from \(i\) when used in a pair kernel.

symbols.name: \(X\)
symbols.def: Pretreatment covariate used for confounding adjustment.

symbols.name: \(P_O\)
symbols.space: probability laws on the space of \(O\)
symbols.def: Observed margin of \(P\) under the map \((X,A,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\mapsto O=(X,A,Y)\).

symbols.name: \(Q_P^{(n)}\)
symbols.space: probability laws on the \(n\)-fold observed-data space
symbols.def: \(Q_P^{(n)}:=P_O^{\otimes n}\), the law under which \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent with common law \(P_O\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal T_{n,M}\)
symbols.def: Set of measurable maps from \((O_1,\ldots,O_n)\) into \([-M,M]\).

symbols.name: \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\)
symbols.def: Estimator to be constructed from \(\mathrm{def:polynomial\text{-}handle}\) in \(\mathrm{oeq:robust\text{-}upper\text{-}construction}\).

symbols.name: \(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\)
symbols.def: Estimator to be constructed from \(\mathrm{def:collision\text{-}handle}\) in \(\mathrm{oeq:robust\text{-}upper\text{-}construction}\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat\tau_n^{\star}\)
symbols.def: Selector map constructed in \(\mathrm{def:total\text{-}estimator}\) from \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\) and \(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\).

assumptions.condition: \(|\mu_{ak}|\le M/2\) for every \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and every \(k\) with \(p_k>0\).

novel.justification: A known scientific scale can center and normalize conditional means to a common interval of width \(M\); bounded monetary contrasts after a prespecified unit conversion and centered bounded scores satisfy this condition even when individual outcomes remain unbounded.

assumptions.condition: \(E_P[(Y-\mu_{ak})^4\mid A=a,X=k]\le M^4\) for every \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and every \(k\) with \(p_k>0\).

novel.justification: The condition permits unbounded outcomes and is satisfied after scale calibration by conditionally bounded, Gaussian, sub-Gaussian, and Student laws with more than four degrees of freedom; it is credible for heavy-tailed financial outcomes whose conditional fourth moments are finite.

standard.name: maximal approximate effect homogeneity with outcome-scale normalization

definitions.name: approximately homogeneous one-unit full-data law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}:=\{P: X\in\{1,\ldots,d\},\ A\in\{0,1\},\ Y,Y(0),Y(1)\in\mathbb R,\ 0<\epsilon<1/2,\ M\ge1,\ 0\le\sigma\le2,\text{ and }P\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:consistency},\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}exchangeability},\mathrm{ass:overlap},\mathrm{ass:mean\text{-}normalization},\mathrm{ass:fourth\text{-}central\text{-}moment},\mathrm{ass:approximate\text{-}homogeneity}\}\).

definitions.name: unrestricted-heterogeneity one-unit full-data law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}:=\{P: X\in\{1,\ldots,d\},\ A\in\{0,1\},\ Y,Y(0),Y(1)\in\mathbb R,\ 0<\epsilon<1/2,\ M\ge1,\text{ and }P\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:consistency},\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}exchangeability},\mathrm{ass:overlap},\mathrm{ass:mean\text{-}normalization},\mathrm{ass:fourth\text{-}central\text{-}moment}\}\).

definitions.name: robust heavy-light ratio-polynomial construction handle
definitions.construction: Split the observations into independent blocks for occupancy classification, coefficient estimation, and marked-outcome evaluation. On light cells, approximate the two reciprocal arm intensities over the overlap cone with a coefficient-controlled polynomial of degree proportional to \(\log(en)\), and evaluate its monomials using cross-block falling-factorial counts paired with robustly truncated or median-aggregated marked sums. On heavy cells, use robust arm-mean ratios. Sum the contributions and apply \(\operatorname{clip}_{[-M,M]}(z):=\max\{-M,\min(M,z)\}\). Determine the degree constant, block proportions, truncation levels, and fixed-sample correction in \(\mathrm{oeq:robust\text{-}upper\text{-}construction}\).

definitions.name: robust collision-weighted construction handle
definitions.construction:
From \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), let \(N_{ak}:=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\}\), \(N_k:=N_{0k}+N_{1k}\), \(S_{ak}:=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\}Y_i\), \(I_k:=\mathbf 1\{N_{0k}N_{1k}>0\}\), and \(R_n:=\sum_{k=1}^dN_kI_k\).  Put \(\overline Y_{ak}:=S_{ak}/N_{ak}\) when \(N_{ak}>0\), and define
\[
 T_n^{\mathrm{col}}:=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M,M]}\!\left(
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{R_n>0\}}{R_n}
 \sum_{k=1}^dN_kI_k(\overline Y_{1k}-\overline Y_{0k})
 \right),
\]
with the inner value defined to be zero when \(R_n=0\).  The map is total, measurable, and computable by one pass through the sample followed by one pass through the occupied categories.

definitions.name: known-radius total selector
definitions.construction: For \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}},T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\in\mathcal T_{n,M}\), let \(u_{n,d}:=d^2/[n^2\log^2(en)]\), \(h_{n,d,\sigma}:=\sigma^2+d/n^2\), and define \[\widehat\tau_n^{\star}:=\begin{cases}T_n^{\mathrm{col}},&h_{n,d,\sigma}\le\min\{1,u_{n,d}\},\\T_n^{\mathrm{poly}},&u_{n,d}<\min\{1,h_{n,d,\sigma}\},\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\] The displayed tie rule makes the selector a total measurable map for every \((n,d,\sigma)\).

definitions.name: radius-indexed least-favorable construction handle
definitions.construction: Begin with scaled two-point outcomes supported on \(\{-M/2,M/2\}\) and propensity values in \([\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\). Use duality between best polynomial approximation and moment matching to choose two Poissonized priors for the marked cell intensities. Couple a common-effect coordinate with centered heterogeneous coordinates bounded by \(\sigma M\), match observable intensity moments through a degree proportional to \(\log(en)\), and transfer the separation to \(Q_P^{(n)}\). Determine the priors, degree constant, centering, normalization, and de-Poissonization in \(\mathrm{oeq:sigma\text{-}indexed\text{-}converse}\).

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\), the causal average treatment effect is identified from \(P_O\) by \(\tau(P)=\sum_{k=1}^{d}p_k\{E_P[Y\mid A=1,X=k]-E_P[Y\mid A=0,X=k]\}\).
statements.justification: This isolates causal identification from the estimation frontier.
statements.gap: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy use the same g-formula, so no new identification claim is made.
statements.consumer: The minimax experiment can target the observed-data functional corresponding to the 401(k) eligibility effect.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\), and write \(S_P:=\{k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}:p_k>0\}\). For \(k\in S_P\), Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:overlap}\) gives
\[
P(A=1,X=k)=p_k\pi_k\ge p_k\epsilon>0,\qquad P(A=0,X=k)=p_k(1-\pi_k)\ge p_k\epsilon>0.
\]
Hence both observed conditional means in cell \(k\) are well-defined and are functionals of \(P_O\). Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:mean\text{-}normalization}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:fourth\text{-}central\text{-}moment}\), which enter through \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\), ensure the needed integrability: conditional Lyapunov's inequality gives
\[
E_P[|Y-\mu_{ak}|\mid A=a,X=k]\le\{E_P[(Y-\mu_{ak})^4\mid A=a,X=k]\}^{1/4}\le M,
\]
and therefore \(E_P[|Y|\mid A=a,X=k]\le 3M/2\). By consistency, for every \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and \(k\in S_P\),
\[
E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=k]=E_P[Y(a)\mid A=a,X=k].
\]
By conditional exchangeability, the right-hand side equals \(E_P[Y(a)\mid X=k]\). Consequently, the law of total expectation over the support of \(X\) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)]
&=\sum_{k\in S_P}p_k\{E_P[Y(1)\mid X=k]-E_P[Y(0)\mid X=k]\}\\
&=\sum_{k\in S_P}p_k\{E_P[Y\mid A=1,X=k]-E_P[Y\mid A=0,X=k]\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
For \(k\notin S_P\), choose arbitrary finite versions of the two conditional means; their contributions are zero because \(p_k=0\). Thus the last display can equivalently be written as a sum from \(1\) to \(d\), independently of those null-cell versions. By \(\mathrm{def:ate\text{-}functional}\), its left-hand side is \(\tau(P)\). Finally, \(p_k=P_O(X=k)\) and, on every positive-mass cell, both conditional means are determined by \(P_O\). Hence the displayed expression is a well-defined observed-law functional and identifies the causal average treatment effect.

statements.statement: Every \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\) satisfies \(|\tau_k|\le M\), \(|\tau(P)|\le M\), and \(\max_{k:p_k>0}|\delta_k|\le2M\). Consequently \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,2}=\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\).
statements.justification: This recomputation makes the radius normalization and unrestricted endpoint exact rather than asserted.
statements.gap: The binary normalization in Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy has the same effect range after centering; the lemma supplies the corresponding continuous-outcome normalization.
statements.consumer: The endpoint proposition and unrestricted comparator now operate on the same law class.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\).  For every positive-mass cell, Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass:mean\text{-}normalization}\) and the triangle inequality give
\[
 |\tau_k|=|\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k}|
 \le |\mu_{1k}|+|\mu_{0k}|
 \le M.
\tag{1}
\]
Because the nonnegative masses sum to one, Definition~\(\mathrm{def:ate\text{-}functional}\) and (1) imply
\[
 |\tau(P)|=\left|\sum_{k=1}^d p_k\tau_k\right|
 \le \sum_{k=1}^d p_k|\tau_k|
 \le M.
\tag{2}
\]
Thus, for every \(k\) with \(p_k>0\),
\[
 |\delta_k|=|\tau_k-\tau(P)|
 \le |\tau_k|+|\tau(P)|
 \le 2M.
\tag{3}
\]
Every member of \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,2}\) is a member of \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\), because the former class imposes all conditions of the latter and one additional condition.  Conversely, (3) shows that every member of \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\) satisfies Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass:approximate\text{-}homogeneity}\) at \(\sigma=2\).  The two classes are therefore equal.  Cells of zero mass play no role in any of these assertions, exactly as required by the support qualifications in the assumptions.

statements.statement: There are constants \(C_{\epsilon},c_{\epsilon}>0\) and explicit estimators \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}},T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\in\mathcal T_{n,M}\) obtained from \(\mathrm{oeq:robust\text{-}upper\text{-}construction}\) such that, uniformly for \(0\le\sigma\le2\) and \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/\log(en)\), the total selector in \(\mathrm{def:total\text{-}estimator}\) obeys \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(\widehat\tau_n^{\star}-\tau(P))^2]\le C_{\epsilon}M^2r_{n,d,\sigma}.\] Relative to the collision guarantee in Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy, Theorem 3 on page 11, the heterogeneity-dependent remainder is never larger in order and is strictly smaller when \(d^2/[n^2\log^2(en)]=o(\sigma^2+d/n^2)\) and \(d=o(n\log(en))\).
statements.justification: The deterministic selector converts two nonnested advantages into the upper envelope of the three-branch frontier.
statements.gap: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy, equation (12) on page 10 and Theorem 3 on page 11, give the collision branch for binary outcomes but do not hand off to the effective-sample-enlargement branch under weak moments.
statements.consumer: For \(n=9915\) and \(d=8196\), the theorem determines whether an approximate-homogeneity claim or unrestricted smoothing controls the 401(k) ATE risk.
statements.proof_tex:
Write
\[
 u:=\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)},\qquad h:=\sigma^2+\frac d{n^2}.
\]
The theorem resolving \(\mathrm{oeq:robust\text{-}upper\text{-}construction}\) supplies
\[
 \sup_PE[(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\{n^{-1}+\min(1,u)\}
\tag{1}
\]
and
\[
 \sup_PE[(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2(n^{-1}+h).
\tag{2}
\]
All suprema here and below are over \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\).

If \(h\le\min\{1,u\}\), Definition~\(\mathrm{def:total\text{-}estimator}\) selects \(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\), and (2) equals the claimed order because \(\min\{1,u,h\}=h\).  If \(u<\min\{1,h\}\), the selector uses \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\); then \(u<1\), and (1) equals the claimed order because \(\min\{1,u,h\}=u\).  If neither inequality holds, then \(\min\{1,u,h\}=1\): if that minimum were smaller than one, either \(h\le u\) would trigger the first case or \(u<h\) would trigger the second.  In the remaining case the selector is zero.  Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:scale\text{-}sanity}\) gives \(|\tau(P)|\le M\), and hence
\[
 E[(0-\tau(P))^2]\le M^2\le M^2\{n^{-1}+\min(1,u,h)\}.
\tag{3}
\]
Equations (1)--(3), with the largest component constant, prove the risk display uniformly over the stated support, radius, and dimension boundaries.

For the comparison clause, the new remainder \(\min\{1,u,h\}\) is always at most the collision remainder \(h\).  If \(d=o(n\log(en))\), then \(u=o(1)\).  If in addition \(u=o(h)\), eventually \(u<\min\{1,h\}\), so the selected remainder is \(u=o(h)\).  This proves the asserted strict order improvement without making an inference or adaptation claim.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there is \(c_{\epsilon}>0\) such that \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\ge c_{\epsilon}M^2/n\) for every \(0\le\sigma\le2\) and every \(d,n\ge1\).
statements.justification: The parametric component must be supplied separately from the large-alphabet fuzzy hypotheses.
statements.gap: This is a standard two-point lower bound; the novel lower-bound content lies in the radius-indexed nonparametric term.
statements.consumer: It prevents the phase diagram from understating ordinary sampling noise in small alphabets.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(h=1/4\).  For \(v\in\{0,1\}\), construct a full-data law \(P_v\) by putting all mass on \(X=1\), drawing \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independently of the potential outcomes, setting \(Y(0)=0\), and setting \(Y(1)=MB_v/2\), where \(B_v\in\{-1,1\}\) and
\[
 P_v(B_v=1)=\frac12+\frac{vh}{\sqrt n}.
\tag{1}
\]
Finally set \(Y=Y(A)\).  The unused \(d-1\) cells have mass zero.  Consistency holds by construction, conditional exchangeability follows from the independence of \(A\), and overlap holds because \(\pi_1=1/2\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\).  The conditional means are \(\mu_{01}=0\) and \(\mu_{11}=vMh/\sqrt n\), so the mean envelope holds.  Moreover \(|Y(a)-E[Y(a)\mid A=a,X=1]|\le M\), and hence the conditional fourth central moment is at most \(M^4\).  There is only one positive-mass cell, so \(\delta_1=0\); thus both laws belong to \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) for every \(0\le\sigma\le2\).  Their targets satisfy
\[
 \Delta_n:=|\tau(P_1)-\tau(P_0)|=\frac{Mh}{\sqrt n}.
\tag{2}
\]

Only a treated response distinguishes the two observed laws.  Direct calculation gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(Q_{P_0}^{(n)}\middle\|Q_{P_1}^{(n)}\right)
 &=-\frac n4\log\left(1-\frac{4h^2}{n}\right)\\
 &\le \frac{h^2}{1-4h^2}\;=\;\frac1{12},
 \end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
where the inequality uses \(-\log(1-x)\le x/(1-x)\) for \(0\le x<1\).  Pinsker's inequality therefore gives total variation at most \(1/\sqrt{24}<1/4\).

For any estimator \(T\), classify the law by whichever of \(\tau(P_0)\) and \(\tau(P_1)\) is closer to \(T\).  A classification error entails squared loss at least \(\Delta_n^2/4\), while the sum of the two testing errors is at least one minus total variation.  Consequently
\[
 \max_{v\in\{0,1\}}E_{Q_{P_v}^{(n)}}[(T-\tau(P_v))^2]
 \ge \frac{\Delta_n^2}{8}\left(1-\frac14\right)
 =\frac{3M^2}{512n}.
\tag{4}
\]
Taking the infimum over \(T\in\mathcal T_{n,M}\) proves the lemma, for example with \(c_{\epsilon}=3/512\).  The construction is valid for every \(d,n\ge1\), including all boundary values of \(\sigma\).

statements.statement:
The two-sided bracket is matched at both required endpoints.  At \(\sigma=0\),
\[
 r_{n,d,0}=n^{-1}+\min\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)},\frac d{n^2}\right\}
 \asymp n^{-1}+\frac d{n^2}
\]
uniformly for \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/\log(en)\).  At \(\sigma=2\),
\(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,2}=\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\) and
\[
 r_{n,d,2}=n^{-1}+\min\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right\}.
\]
The lower expression in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:two\text{-}sided\text{-}minimax\text{-}bracket}\) is of the same order as these two rates at \(\sigma=0\) and \(\sigma=2\), respectively.
statements.proof_tex:
Write
\[
 L:=\log(en),\qquad
 u:=\frac{d^2}{n^2L^2},\qquad
 q:=\frac d{n^2}.
\tag{1}
\]
We may take the dimension-range constant in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:two\text{-}sided\text{-}minimax\text{-}bracket}\) to satisfy \(c_{\epsilon}\le1\).  Thus the stipulated range implies
\[
 q\le\frac{c_{\epsilon}}L\le1.
\tag{2}
\]
For every integer \(n\ge1\), \(L^2\le4n\): indeed, \(\log n\le\sqrt n\) and \(1+\sqrt n\le2\sqrt n\).

At \(\sigma=0\), the definition of \(r_{n,d,\sigma}\) gives
\[
 r_{n,d,0}=\frac1n+\min\{1,u,q\}.
\tag{3}
\]
If \(d\ge L^2\), then \(u=q(d/L^2)\ge q\), and (2) shows that the minimum in (3) is \(q\).  If \(d<L^2\), then
\[
 q<\frac{L^2}{n^2}\le\frac4n.
\tag{4}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \frac15\left(\frac1n+q\right)
 \le \frac1n
 \le r_{n,d,0}
 \le \frac1n+q.
\tag{5}
\]
Equations (3)--(5) prove uniformly that
\[
 r_{n,d,0}\asymp \frac1n+\frac d{n^2}.
\tag{6}
\]
At this endpoint the lower benchmark in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:two\text{-}sided\text{-}minimax\text{-}bracket}\) is exactly \(n^{-1}+q\), so the bracket is order-matched.

At \(\sigma=2\), \(4+q\ge1\), and therefore
\[
 r_{n,d,2}=\frac1n+\min\{1,u\}.
\tag{7}
\]
Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:scale\text{-}sanity}\) gives the support-qualified class identity
\[
 \mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,2}=\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}.
\tag{8}
\]
Let \(m:=\min\{1,u\}\).  The normalized lower benchmark at this endpoint is
\[
 B:=\frac1n+q+4m.
\tag{9}
\]
If \(d\ge L^2\), then \(q\le m\): when \(u\le1\), this follows from \(q\le u=m\), and when \(u>1\), it follows from (2) and \(m=1\).  Hence \(B\le5(n^{-1}+m)\).  If \(d<L^2\), (4) gives
\[
 B\le\frac5n+4m\le5\left(\frac1n+m\right).
\tag{10}
\]
Conversely, \(B\ge n^{-1}+m\).  Equations (7), (9), and (10) show
\[
 B\asymp r_{n,d,2}.
\tag{11}
\]
The common factor \(M^2\) does not affect order equivalence.  Equations (6), (8), and (11) prove both endpoint claims uniformly over the stipulated nonempty theorem range and for arbitrary zero-mass cells.  Nothing in the argument compares the benchmarks uniformly at shrinking interior radii.
statements.justification: The explicit algebra and class equality are the well-posedness sanity check for the interpolating theorem.
statements.gap: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy establish the two binary endpoint benchmarks in Theorems 2--4; the new content is their same-class radius-indexed interpolation for real outcomes.
statements.consumer: Readers can compare the phase diagram with the two familiar benchmarks without silently changing the outcome normalization.

statements.statement:
The answer to the robust upper-construction question is affirmative.  For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), the explicit linear-mark Chebyshev factorial estimator \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\) in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:continuous\text{-}ratio\text{-}polynomial\text{-}upper}\) and the occupancy-weighted estimator \(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\) in \(\mathrm{def:collision\text{-}handle}\) are elements of \(\mathcal T_{n,M}\).  There are \(C_{\epsilon},c_{\epsilon}>0\) such that, for every \(0\le\sigma\le2\) and \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/\log(en)\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\left\{n^{-1}+\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)\right\}
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\left(n^{-1}+\sigma^2+\frac d{n^2}\right).
\]
Both maps have explicit zero fallbacks and clipping, and neither bound contains an additional logarithmic factor.
statements.proof_tex:
Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:continuous\text{-}ratio\text{-}polynomial\text{-}upper}\) constructs the explicit linear-mark Chebyshev factorial estimator \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\) as a measurable sample map, supplies its zero fallbacks and clipping, and proves uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) that
\[
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_\epsilon M^2\left\{n^{-1}+
 \min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)\right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Its clipping shows directly that \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\in\mathcal T_{n,M}\).

Next define \(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\) by Definition~\(\mathrm{def:collision\text{-}handle}\).  This is exactly the total map denoted by \(T_n^{\mathrm{occ}}\) in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:continuous\text{-}occupancy\text{-}collision\text{-}upper}\): empirical arm means are evaluated only when both arm counts are positive, the outer ratio is evaluated only when \(R_n>0\), the remaining cases use the specified zero value, and the result is clipped into \([-M,M]\).  Hence \(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\in\mathcal T_{n,M}\), and that lemma gives
\[
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_\epsilon M^2\left(n^{-1}+\sigma^2+\frac d{n^2}\right).
\tag{2}
\]
Take \(c_\epsilon\) to be the smaller of the positive dimension constants in the two lemmas and enlarge \(C_\epsilon\) to dominate both constants.  Then (1)--(2) hold simultaneously for every \(0\le\sigma\le2\) and \(1\le d\le c_\epsilon n^2/\log(en)\).  The arguments include \(\sigma=0\), \(\sigma=2\), empty empirical treatment arms, and \(R_n=0\).  Since the rates in (1)--(2) are exactly the displayed rates, neither construction incurs an additional logarithmic factor.
statements.justification: The explicit linear-mark lift and occupancy estimator close both real-outcome upper branches without an extra logarithm.
statements.gap: The construction extends the binary heavy-light and collision architectures to real outcomes under the stated conditional fourth-moment envelope.
statements.consumer: It supplies the two data-driven inputs used by the known-radius selector.

statements.statement:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there is \(c_{\epsilon}>0\) such that, uniformly over \(0\le\sigma\le2\) and \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/\log(en)\), the same model admits the radius-indexed lower bound
\[
 \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \ge c_{\epsilon}M^2\left\{
 \frac1n+\frac d{n^2}+\sigma^2\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)
 \right\}.
\]
The radius-dependent family is obtained by passing the fixed-sample binary one-arm hard experiment through the hypothesis-independent channel
\[
 B\longmapsto B'\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}\!\left(\frac12+\frac\sigma2\left(B-\frac12\right)\right),
 \qquad Y=M(B'-1/2).
\]
This construction has realization-wise radius at most \(\sigma M\) and preserves total-variation control by data processing.  It yields the natural product term \(\sigma^2\min\{1,d^2/[n^2\log^2(en)]\}\); it does not establish the stronger interior term \(\min\{\sigma^2,d^2/[n^2\log^2(en)]\}\).
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(\lambda=\sigma/2\in[0,1]\).  Start from the binary one-arm subclass in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:zeng\text{-}binary\text{-}one\text{-}arm\text{-}lower}\), with treated response \(B\in\{0,1\}\), treated cell mean \(\eta_k\in[0,1]\), and control response identically zero.  Conditional on every binary potential response \(B(a)\), independently draw
\[
 B'(a)\mid B(a)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}\!\left\{\frac12+\lambda\left(B(a)-\frac12\right)\right\},
 \qquad Y(a)=M\{B'(a)-1/2\},
\tag{1}
\]
and set \(Y=Y(A)\).  The randomization in (1) is independent of treatment conditional on the original potential outcomes and \(X\), so Assumptions~\(\mathrm{ass:consistency}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}exchangeability}\) are preserved.  Propensities and cell masses are unchanged, hence Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass:overlap}\) is preserved.

For the control and treated arms, respectively,
\[
 \mu_{0k}=-\frac{M\lambda}{2},
 \qquad
 \mu_{1k}=M\lambda(\eta_k-1/2).
\tag{2}
\]
Both means lie in \([-M/2,M/2]\).  Since \(Y(a)\in\{-M/2,M/2\}\), the absolute centered outcome is at most \(M\), so every conditional fourth central moment is at most \(M^4\).  Equations (2) give
\[
 \tau_k=M\lambda\eta_k,
 \qquad
 \tau(P)=M\lambda\sum_{k=1}^dp_k\eta_k.
\tag{3}
\]
Writing \(\psi:=\sum_kp_k\eta_k\),
\[
 |\tau_k-\tau(P)|=M\lambda|\eta_k-\psi|\le M\lambda\le\sigma M.
\tag{4}
\]
Thus every transformed law belongs to \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\).  The verification is realization-wise, includes \(\sigma=0\), and imposes no condition on zero-mass cells.

The transformation from \((X,A,B)\) to \((X,A,Y)\) is a Markov kernel identical under the two fuzzy hypotheses.  Total variation between the induced mixtures can only decrease under this kernel.  Equivalently, for \(\lambda>0\), any estimator \(T\) in the transformed experiment can be applied after simulating (1) from the source sample, and \(T/(M\lambda)\) estimates \(\psi\).  Conditional expectation given the source sample can only reduce squared loss.  Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:zeng\text{-}binary\text{-}one\text{-}arm\text{-}lower}\) therefore gives, for \(d\le b_{\epsilon}n\log n\),
\[
 \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \ge c_{\epsilon}M^2\lambda^2\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right\}.
\tag{5}
\]
For \(d>b_{\epsilon}n\log n\), take \(d_0=\lfloor b_{\epsilon}n\log n\rfloor\) and embed the \(d_0\)-cell construction by assigning zero mass to the remaining cells.  After decreasing the dimension constant and absorbing fixed cutoffs, (5) implies
\[
 \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \ge c_{\epsilon}M^2\sigma^2
 \min\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right\}.
\tag{6}
\]
At \(\lambda=0\), (6) is the zero inequality.

Independently, Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:scaled\text{-}binary\text{-}exact\text{-}lower\text{-}transfer}\) yields throughout the stated range
\[
 \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \ge c_{\epsilon}M^2\left(\frac1n+\frac d{n^2}\right).
\tag{7}
\]
The maximum of the right sides of (6) and (7) is at least half their sum, which proves the theorem's displayed lower bound.  The finitely many sample sizes below the source lemmas' cutoffs are absorbed by decreasing \(c_{\epsilon}\): the displayed bracket divided by \(n^{-1}\) is then uniformly bounded on the stipulated dimension and radius ranges, while Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:parametric\text{-}lower}\) supplies a fixed multiple of \(M^2/n\).

Finally, (3) shows that the target separation is exactly \(M\lambda\) times the source separation.  A source separation of order \(\min\{1,d/[n\log(en)]\}\) therefore becomes \(M\sigma\min\{1,d/[n\log(en)]\}\) up to constants, and its square is precisely the product term in (6).  Hence this channel proves no standalone interior separation of order \(M\min\{\sigma,d/[n\log(en)]\}\).
statements.justification: The hypothesis-independent channel gives a rigorous same-class radius-indexed converse and exposes the product scaling forced by this contraction.
statements.gap: The construction does not supply the stronger standalone interior-radius separation requested by the original open question.
statements.consumer: It yields the honest lower side of the minimax bracket while preserving both endpoint rates.

statements.statement:
The answer is complete for fixed interior radii but remains partial for a radius allowed to shrink with \(n\).  For every fixed \(s\in(0,2]\), there are constants \(0<c_{\epsilon,s}\le C_{\epsilon,s}<\infty\) such that, uniformly over \(s\le\sigma\le2\) and \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/\log(en)\),
\[
 c_{\epsilon,s}M^2r_{n,d,\sigma}
 \le \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \le C_{\epsilon,s}M^2r_{n,d,\sigma}.
\]
The same equivalence holds with constants independent of \(\sigma\in[0,2]\) whenever either
\[
 \frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\ge1
 \qquad\text{or}\qquad
 d\le\log^2(en).
\]
Thus the product lower remainder is minimax-tight at every fixed interior radius.  The frozen bounds do not, however, decide the fully uniform shrinking-radius problem.  Indeed, with \(L_n:=\log(en)\), \(d_n:=n\), and \(\sigma_n:=L_n^{-1/2}\), the selector benchmark divided by the proved lower benchmark satisfies
\[
 \frac{n^{-1}+\min\{1,d_n^2/(n^2L_n^2),\sigma_n^2+d_n/n^2\}}
 {n^{-1}+d_n/n^2+\sigma_n^2\min\{1,d_n^2/(n^2L_n^2)\}}
 \asymp L_n\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Consequently a uniform resolution still requires either a stronger constrained converse or a sharper estimator in the triangular regime \(\sigma_n\to0\), \(\log^2(en)<d<n\log(en)\); neither endpoint-only reasoning nor the existing radius channel decides between them.
statements.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 L:=\log(en),\qquad
 u:=\frac{d^2}{n^2L^2},\qquad
 x:=\frac d{n^2},\qquad
 v:=\min\{1,u\}.
\]
Define the normalized upper and lower benchmarks
\[
 q:=\frac1n+\min\{v,\sigma^2+x\},
 \qquad
 \ell:=\frac1n+x+\sigma^2v.
\tag{1}
\]
By the definition of \(r_{n,d,\sigma}\), \(q=r_{n,d,\sigma}\).  Theorems~\(\mathrm{thm:frontier\text{-}upper}\) and \(\mathrm{thm:radius\text{-}channel\text{-}converse}\), respectively, give constants depending only on \(\epsilon\) such that
\[
 \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\le C_{\epsilon}M^2q,
 \qquad
 \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\ge c_{\epsilon}M^2\ell.
\tag{2}
\]
The support, overlap, moment, radius, and dimension conditions in (2) are exactly those of the two cited theorems.  The remaining argument is deterministic.

Fix \(s\in(0,2]\) and suppose \(s\le\sigma\le2\).  Since a minimum is no larger than either argument,
\[
 q\le\frac1n+v.
\tag{3}
\]
Since \(\sigma^2\ge s^2\) and \(x\ge0\),
\[
 \ell\ge\frac1n+s^2v.
\tag{4}
\]
Combining (3)--(4),
\[
 q\le\max\{1,s^{-2}\}\ell.
\tag{5}
\]
The lower inequality in (2) and (5) give
\[
 \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \ge \frac{c_{\epsilon}}{\max\{1,s^{-2}\}}M^2q,
\]
while the upper inequality in (2) gives the reverse comparison.  This proves matching for every fixed lower radius \(s>0\), including the boundaries \(d=1\), \(d=c_{\epsilon}n^2/L\), \(\sigma=s\), and \(\sigma=2\).

If \(u\ge1\), then \(v=1\).  When \(\sigma^2+x\le1\), (1) gives \(q=\ell\).  When \(\sigma^2+x>1\),
\[
 q=\frac1n+1<\frac1n+x+\sigma^2=\ell.
\]
The dimension range, after taking \(c_{\epsilon}\le1\), also gives
\[
 x=\frac d{n^2}\le\frac{c_{\epsilon}}L\le1.
\]
Together with \(n^{-1}\le1\) and \(\sigma^2\le4\),
\[
 q\le\ell\le6\le6q.
\tag{6}
\]
Thus (2) and (6) prove uniform matching in the saturation regime \(u\ge1\).

If \(d\le L^2\), then
\[
 u=\frac{d^2}{n^2L^2}\le\frac d{n^2}=x,
\]
so \(v\le x\).  Therefore
\[
 q\le\frac1n+v\le\frac1n+x\le\ell.
\tag{7}
\]
Equations (2) and (7) prove uniform matching in the small-alphabet regime.

It remains to test whether the two established benchmarks are uniformly comparable over all shrinking radii.  Let \(n\to\infty\), set \(d_n=n\), put \(L_n=\log(en)\), and take \(\sigma_n=L_n^{-1/2}\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(0<\sigma_n<2\), the dimension condition holds, and
\[
 u_n=L_n^{-2},\qquad x_n=n^{-1},\qquad \sigma_n^2=L_n^{-1}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 q_n=\frac1n+\min\{L_n^{-2},L_n^{-1}+n^{-1}\}
 =\frac1n+L_n^{-2}\asymp L_n^{-2},
\tag{8}
\]
whereas
\[
 \ell_n=\frac2n+L_n^{-1}L_n^{-2}
 =\frac2n+L_n^{-3}\asymp L_n^{-3}.
\tag{9}
\]
Dividing (8) by (9) gives \(q_n/\ell_n\asymp L_n\to\infty\).  Since eventually \(L_n^2<d_n<nL_n\), the witness lies in the stated triangular regime.  This proves the localization claim: fixed interior radii and the two displayed dimension regimes are settled, but the proved bounds alone do not settle the fully uniform shrinking-radius problem.  No inference, coverage, or adaptation to unknown \(M\) or \(\sigma\) is asserted.
statements.justification: This gives the strongest rate conclusion that follows from the proved same-class upper and lower bounds and localizes the unresolved part to shrinking radii.
statements.gap: The established bounds match at every fixed interior radius, but their numerical benchmarks separate along an explicit shrinking-radius sequence.
statements.consumer: A future constrained fuzzy-hypothesis or calibrated-estimator argument need only address the localized triangular regime.

statements.statement:
For \(N_{ak}:=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\}\), \(N_k:=N_{0k}+N_{1k}\), \(I_k:=\mathbf 1\{N_{0k}N_{1k}>0\}\), and \(R_n:=\sum_{k=1}^dN_kI_k\), fixed overlap implies that constants \(b_{\epsilon},B_{\epsilon}>0\) satisfy
\[
 Q_P^{(n)}(R_n=0)\le2\exp\left\{-b_{\epsilon}\frac{n^2}{n\vee d}\right\}
\]
and
\[
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\left[\frac{\mathbf 1\{R_n>0\}}{R_n}\right]
 \le B_{\epsilon}\left\{\frac{n\vee d}{n^2}+\exp\left(-b_{\epsilon}\frac{n^2}{n\vee d}\right)\right\}.
\]

statements.statement:
Define \(N_{ak}\), \(N_k\), \(I_k\), and \(R_n\) as in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:zeng\text{-}usable\text{-}occupancy\text{-}reciprocal}\), put \(S_{ak}:=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\}Y_i\), and set \(\overline Y_{ak}:=S_{ak}/N_{ak}\) when \(N_{ak}>0\).  The explicit total estimator
\[
 T_n^{\mathrm{occ}}:=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M,M]}\!\left(
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{R_n>0\}}{R_n}
 \sum_{k=1}^dN_kI_k(\overline Y_{1k}-\overline Y_{0k})
 \right),
\]
with inner value zero when \(R_n=0\), satisfies, for constants \(C_{\epsilon},c_{\epsilon}>0\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T_n^{\mathrm{occ}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\left(\frac1n+\sigma^2+\frac d{n^2}\right)
\]
whenever \(0\le\sigma\le2\) and \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/\log(en)\).
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(\widetilde T_n\) denote the expression inside the clipping operation.  By Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:scale\text{-}sanity}\), \(\tau(P)\in[-M,M]\); projection onto this interval therefore cannot increase squared loss, so it suffices to control \(\widetilde T_n\).

Let \(\mathcal G=\sigma((X_i,A_i)_{i=1}^n)\).  Conditional independence of the outcomes and the definitions of the cell means give
\[
 E[\widetilde T_n\mid\mathcal G]
 =\frac{\mathbf 1\{R_n>0\}}{R_n}\sum_{k=1}^dN_kI_k\tau_k.
\tag{1}
\]
On \(\{R_n>0\}\), subtracting \(\tau(P)\) from (1) produces a convex combination of the \(\delta_k\)'s, whose absolute value is at most \(\sigma M\).  On \(\{R_n=0\}\), the absolute error of the conditional mean is \(|\tau(P)|\le M\).  Hence
\[
 E\!\left[\{E[\widetilde T_n\mid\mathcal G]-\tau(P)\}^2\right]
 \le M^2\{\sigma^2+Q_P^{(n)}(R_n=0)\}.
\tag{2}
\]

Write \(v_{ak}=\operatorname{Var}(Y\mid A=a,X=k)\).  Lyapunov's inequality and Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass:fourth\text{-}central\text{-}moment}\) imply \(v_{ak}\le M^2\).  Thus
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(\widetilde T_n\mid\mathcal G)
 \le \frac{M^2\mathbf 1\{R_n>0\}}{R_n^2}
 \sum_{k=1}^dN_k^2I_k\left(\frac1{N_{1k}}+\frac1{N_{0k}}\right).
\tag{3}
\]

It remains to average (3) over treatment assignment.  Conditional on the category counts, \(N_{1k}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(N_k,\pi_k)\), independently across \(k\).  If \(V\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(m,\pi)\), \(m\ge2\), and \(J=\mathbf 1\{0<V<m\}\), then
\[
 E\left[\frac1V\,\middle|\,J=1\right]
 \le \frac{2}{(m+1)\pi\{1-\pi^m-(1-\pi)^m\}}
 \le \frac{C_{\epsilon}}m.
\tag{4}
\]
Indeed, \(1/v\le2/(v+1)\) for \(v\ge1\),
\[
 E[(V+1)^{-1}]=\frac{1-(1-\pi)^{m+1}}{(m+1)\pi},
\]
and \(1-\pi^m-(1-\pi)^m\ge2\pi(1-\pi)\ge2\epsilon(1-\epsilon)\).  The same bound applies to \(1/(m-V)\).  Conditional on the category counts and the indicators \((I_k)_k\), the quantity \(R_n\) is fixed.  Applying (4) termwise in (3) therefore yields
\[
 E[\operatorname{Var}(\widetilde T_n\mid\mathcal G)\mid (N_k,I_k)_k]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\frac{\mathbf 1\{R_n>0\}}{R_n}.
\tag{5}
\]

Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:zeng\text{-}usable\text{-}occupancy\text{-}reciprocal}\), (2), (5), and the conditional bias--variance identity now give
\[
 E[(\widetilde T_n-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\left\{\sigma^2+\frac{n\vee d}{n^2}
 +\exp\left(-b_{\epsilon}\frac{n^2}{n\vee d}\right)\right\}.
\tag{6}
\]
If \(d\le n\), the exponential in (6) is at most \(C_{\epsilon}/n\).  If \(n<d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/\log(en)\), decrease \(c_{\epsilon}\), if necessary, so that the same exponential is at most \(C_{\epsilon}d/n^2\).  Finally \((n\vee d)/n^2\le n^{-1}+d/n^2\).  These observations turn (6) into the asserted bound.  All divisions occur only on \(I_k=1\) or \(R_n>0\); the displayed fallback covers their boundaries.

statements.statement:
Fix \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).  Let \(\mathcal H_{n,d}^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) be the fixed-sample binary-outcome experiment with \(p_k=1/d\), \(\epsilon\le\pi_k\le1-\epsilon\), conditional response means in \([0,1]\), and a common cell treatment effect, and write \(\psi(P):=d^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^d(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})\).  There are constants \(a_{\epsilon},b_{\epsilon}>0\) and \(N_{\epsilon}<\infty\) such that, for \(n\ge N_{\epsilon}\) and \(d\le b_{\epsilon}n^2\),
\[
 \inf_{\widehat\psi}\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal H_{n,d}^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)}
 E_P[(\widehat\psi-\psi(P))^2]
 \ge a_{\epsilon}\left(\frac1n+\frac d{n^2}\right).
\]

attestation.note: The theorem states the uniform-mass exact-effect-homogeneity minimax lower rate, and Appendix C.8 supplies the fixed-sample fuzzy-hypothesis construction.

statements.statement:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are constants \(a_{\epsilon},b_{\epsilon}>0\) and \(N_{\epsilon}<\infty\) such that, for \(n\ge N_{\epsilon}\), \(d\le b_{\epsilon}n^2\), and every \(0\le\sigma\le2\),
\[
 \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \ge a_{\epsilon}M^2\left(\frac1n+\frac d{n^2}\right).
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Take any binary law in \(\mathcal H_{n,d}^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\), write its binary potential outcomes as \(B(0),B(1)\), and define
\[
 Y(a)=M\{B(a)-1/2\},\qquad Y=Y(A).
\tag{1}
\]
If the source law is initially specified only through its observed conditional Bernoulli distributions, augment it by drawing \(B(0),B(1)\) conditionally on \(X\), independently of \(A\), with the prescribed arm means.  This gives consistency and conditional exchangeability without changing the observed experiment.  Overlap is unchanged.  Since \(Y(a)\in\{-M/2,M/2\}\), its conditional mean lies in \([-M/2,M/2]\) and its centered fourth moment is at most \(M^4\).  The cell effects and the ATE are multiplied by \(M\); exact homogeneity is preserved, so the resulting law belongs to \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) for every \(\sigma\ge0\).

The observed transformation \(B=Y/M+1/2\) is invertible.  Consequently, every \(T\in\mathcal T_{n,M}\) induces the binary estimator \(T/M\), and
\[
 E[(T-\tau(P))^2]=M^2E[(T/M-\psi(P^{\mathrm{bin}}))^2].
\tag{2}
\]
Restricting the supremum in Definition~\(\mathrm{def:minimax\text{-}risk}\) to these scaled laws, taking the infimum over \(T\), and applying Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:zeng\text{-}binary\text{-}exact\text{-}homogeneity\text{-}lower}\) proves the claim.

statements.statement:
Fix \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).  In the fixed-sample binary-outcome model with arbitrary cell masses, overlap \(\epsilon\le\pi_k\le1-\epsilon\), arbitrary treated response means in \([0,1]\), and control response identically zero, constants \(a_{\epsilon},b_{\epsilon}>0\) and \(N_{\epsilon}<\infty\) satisfy, for \(n\ge N_{\epsilon}\) and \(d\le b_{\epsilon}n\log n\),
\[
 \inf_{\widehat\psi}\sup_P E_P[(\widehat\psi-\sum_{k=1}^dp_k\mu_{1k})^2]
 \ge a_{\epsilon}\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2 n}\right\}.
\]

statements.statement:
Let \(V:=Y/M\), \(s_{ak}:=P(X=k,A=a)\), and \(z_{ak}:=E_P[V\mathbf 1\{X=k,A=a\}]\).  Consider a block of \(m\) independent observations and, for integers \(K\ge2\), numbers \(B>0\), and
\[
 g_{Kj}:=(-1)^j\frac{2^{2j+3}}{K(K+j+2)}\binom{K+j+2}{2j+4},\qquad 0\le j\le K-2,
\]
define the ordered, distinct-index statistic
\[
 U_{k,a,j}:=\frac{1}{(m)_{j+2}}
 \sum_{i_0,\ldots,i_{j+1}\ {\rm distinct}}
 V_{i_0}\mathbf 1\{X_{i_0}=k,A_{i_0}=a\}
 \mathbf 1\{X_{i_1}=k\}
 \prod_{t=2}^{j+1}\mathbf 1\{X_{i_t}=k,A_{i_t}=a\},
\]
and
\[
 \widehat P_k:=\sum_{j=0}^{K-2}\frac{g_{Kj}}{B^{j+1}}
 \{U_{k,1,j}-U_{k,0,j}\}.
\]
If \(S\subseteq\{k:p_k\le B/4\}\) is deterministic, \(4(K+2)^2\le m\), and \(4(K+2)/m\le3B/4\), then
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{Q_P^{(m)}}\!\left(\sum_{k\in S}\widehat P_k\right)
 \le \frac{C_{\epsilon}}m+C_{\epsilon}6^{2K}
 \left\{dB^2+\frac{d^2K^2B^2}{m}\right\}.
\]
The conclusion holds for every \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\); no boundedness of \(Y\) is required.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\).  Put \(\nu_{ak}:=\mu_{ak}/M\).  Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass:mean\text{-}normalization}\) gives \(|\nu_{ak}|\le1/2\).  Lyapunov's inequality and Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass:fourth\text{-}central\text{-}moment}\) give
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_P(V\mid A=a,X=k)
 \le \{E_P[(V-\nu_{ak})^4\mid A=a,X=k]\}^{1/2}\le1.
\]
Consequently
\[
 E_P[V^2\mathbf 1\{X=k,A=a\}]
 =s_{ak}\{\operatorname{Var}(V\mid A=a,X=k)+\nu_{ak}^2\}
 \le\frac54s_{ak}.
\tag{1}
\]
This is the only moment inequality needed for a repeated marked selector.

The distinct-index definition and independence show directly that
\[
 E_P[U_{k,a,j}]=z_{ak}p_ks_{ak}^{j}.
\tag{2}
\]
We next give the covariance count.  Multiply two ordered sums defining \(U_{k,a,j}\) and \(U_{\ell,b,r}\), and partition the product according to the partial matching between their two ordered index tuples.  A matching of size \(h\) leaves \(j+r+4-h\) distinct sample indices.  Since \(j+2,r+2\le K\), cancellation of falling factorials and \(4K^2\le m\) give
\[
 \frac{(m)_{j+r+4-h}}{(m)_{j+2}(m)_{r+2}}
 \le \frac{e}{m^h}.
\tag{3}
\]
The number of matchings of size \(h\) is at most \(K^{2h}/h!\).  If no two marked positions are identified, all repeated factors are indicators and the usual falling-factorial identity applies.  If one marked position is identified with an unmarked position, the corresponding expectation is \(z_{ak}\) or zero and satisfies \(|z_{ak}|\le s_{ak}/2\).  The two marked positions can be identified only when \(k=\ell\) and \(a=b\); their expectation is then bounded by (1).  Thus every overlap term is bounded by the same nonnegative coefficient calculation as for unmarked factorial monomials, except for a factor at most \(5/4\) on the common marked selector.

For completeness, the coefficient calculation is as follows.  Define
\[
 G_K(x):=\sum_{j=0}^{K-2}g_{Kj}x^j.
\]
The alternating signs imply that its absolute-coefficient majorant is \(G_K^+(x):=G_K(-x)\).  From the Chebyshev identity
\[
 G_K^+(x)=\frac{T_K(1+2x)-1-2K^2x}{2K^2x^2}
\]
and the closed form for \(T_K(t)\) on \(t\ge1\),
\[
 G_K^+(x)\le6^K\max\{1,x^{K-2}\},\qquad x\ge0.
\tag{4}
\]
Because \(p_k\le B/4\) on \(S\) and \(4K/m\le3B/4\), every intensity vector arising after the overlap replacements has total mass at most \(B\).  Summing the absolute values of the overlap terms in (3) against the coefficients and applying (4) therefore gives the following three contributions.  The matching containing the two marked positions is, by (1), Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass:overlap}\), and \(\sum_{k,a}s_{ak}=1\), at most \(C_{\epsilon}/m\).  All remaining within-category matchings are at most \(C_{\epsilon}6^{2K}dB^2\).  For distinct categories an overlap is impossible; subtracting the product of expectations leaves only the finite-population falling-factorial correction, and
\[
 \left|\frac{(m)_{j+r+4}}{(m)_{j+2}(m)_{r+2}}-1\right|
 \le \frac{2K^2}{m},
\tag{5}
\]
so their total is at most \(C_{\epsilon}6^{2K}d^2K^2B^2/m\).  Adding these three bounds proves the display.  Equations (1)--(5) also show explicitly why a fourth central moment is more than sufficient: the proof uses only the induced conditional second moment of the single linear mark, and never multiplies two outcomes unless their marked sample indices coincide.
statements.justification: This isolates the only new weak-moment covariance step in the continuous-outcome polynomial lift.
statements.gap: Unlike a bounded binary mark, a real mark can overlap itself; the displayed second-moment calculation controls exactly that case.

statements.statement:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are \(C_{\epsilon},\rho_{\epsilon}>0\) and a finite \(N_{\epsilon}\) for which the following explicit total estimator is defined.  Put \(L=\log(en)\), split the sample into \(I_0=\{1,\ldots,\lfloor n/2\rfloor\}\) and its complement \(I_1\), and write \(m_j=|I_j|\).  Set
\[
 \lambda_0=256,\quad b_0=4096,\quad D_6=8\log(27/4),\quad
 \alpha_0=\min\left\{1,\frac1{64\log6},\frac1{512D_6}\right\}.
\]
When \(n\ge N_{\epsilon}\) and \(d\le\rho_{\epsilon}nL\), set \(K=\lfloor\alpha_0L\rfloor\ge2\), \(B=b_0L/m_1\), classify
\[
 \widehat{\mathcal H}:=\left\{k:\sum_{i\in I_0}\mathbf 1\{X_i=k\}>\lambda_0L\right\},
 \qquad \widehat{\mathcal L}:=\widehat{\mathcal H}^{c},
\]
use the statistics \(\widehat P_k\) of Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:linear\text{-}mark\text{-}factorial\text{-}covariance}\) on block \(I_1\), and put
\[
 \widehat h_k:=\frac{N_k^{(1)}}{m_1}\left\{
 \frac{\sum_{i\in I_1}V_i\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=1\}}{N_{1k}^{(1)}}\mathbf 1\{N_{1k}^{(1)}>0\}
 -\frac{\sum_{i\in I_1}V_i\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=0\}}{N_{0k}^{(1)}}\mathbf 1\{N_{0k}^{(1)}>0\}
 \right\}.
\]
Define
\[
 T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}:=M\operatorname{clip}_{[-1,1]}\!\left(
 \sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}}\widehat h_k+
 \sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}\widehat P_k\right).
\]
When \(n<N_{\epsilon}\) or \(d>\rho_{\epsilon}nL\), set \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}=0\).  Then, for every \(0\le\sigma\le2\) and every \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/L\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\left\{\frac1n+\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2L^2}\right)\right\}.
\]
The estimator uses \(O(dK^2)\) arithmetic operations after cell aggregation and has bounded fallbacks on every division boundary.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) and work first in normalized outcome units.  Put
\[
 V:=Y/M,\qquad \nu_{ak}:=\mu_{ak}/M,\qquad
 s_{ak}:=P(X=k,A=a),\qquad z_{ak}:=E_P[V\mathbf 1\{X=k,A=a\}],
\]
and
\[
 \varphi_k:=p_k(\nu_{1k}-\nu_{0k}).
\]
Then \(z_{ak}=s_{ak}\nu_{ak}\) and, by Definition~\(\mathrm{def:ate\text{-}functional}\),
\[
 \frac{\tau(P)}M=\sum_{k=1}^d\varphi_k.
\tag{1}
\]
Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass:mean\text{-}normalization}\) gives \(|\nu_{ak}|\le1/2\).  Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass:overlap}\) gives \(s_{ak}\ge\epsilon p_k\) on every positive-mass cell.  Lyapunov's inequality and Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass:fourth\text{-}central\text{-}moment}\) also give
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_P(V\mid A=a,X=k)
 \le \{E_P[(V-\nu_{ak})^4\mid A=a,X=k]\}^{1/2}\le1.
\tag{2}
\]
Thus all marked statistics below have finite second moments.  Zero-mass cells contribute zero and need no conditional quantity.

We first establish the approximation identity.  Let \(T_K\) be the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind and define, with polynomial continuation at zero,
\[
 H_K(x):=\frac{1-T_K(1-2x)}{2K^2},\qquad
 E_K(x):=\frac{H_K(x)}x,\qquad
 G_K(x):=\frac{1-E_K(x)}x.
\]
Expanding the shifted Chebyshev polynomial gives
\[
 G_K(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{K-2}(-1)^j
 \frac{2^{2j+3}}{K(K+j+2)}\binom{K+j+2}{2j+4}x^j
 =\sum_{j=0}^{K-2}g_{Kj}x^j.
\tag{3}
\]
For \(0\le x\le1\), the elementary inequality \(|T_K(1-2x)|\le1\) implies
\[
 0\le x\{1-xG_K(x)\}=H_K(x)\le K^{-2}.
\tag{4}
\]
If \(p_k\le B\), then \(0\le s_{ak}/B\le1\).  Using \(|z_{ak}|\le s_{ak}/2\), \(s_{ak}\ge\epsilon p_k\), and (4), we obtain
\[
 \left|p_k\nu_{ak}-\frac{p_kz_{ak}}B
 G_K(s_{ak}/B)\right|
 \le \frac{B}{2\epsilon K^2}.
\tag{5}
\]
The distinct-index identity in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:linear\text{-}mark\text{-}factorial\text{-}covariance}\) states that
\[
 E_P[U_{k,a,j}]=z_{ak}p_ks_{ak}^{j}.
\]
Consequently, (3) shows that \(\widehat P_k\) is unbiased for
\[
 \frac{p_kz_{1k}}B G_K(s_{1k}/B)
 -\frac{p_kz_{0k}}B G_K(s_{0k}/B).
\tag{6}
\]

We next control the independent pilot classification.  Write
\[
 B_-:=\frac{\lambda_0L}{2m_0},\qquad
 B_+:=\frac{2\lambda_0L}{m_0}
\]
and let
\[
 \mathcal A:=
 \left\{\widehat{\mathcal H}\subseteq\{k:p_k\ge B_-\},\quad
 \widehat{\mathcal L}\subseteq\{k:p_k\le B_+\}\right\}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), the balanced split and \(b_0=16\lambda_0\) imply \(B_+\le B/4\).  If \(p_k<B_-\), the pilot count has mean less than \(\lambda_0L/2\); if \(p_k>B_+\), its mean exceeds \(2\lambda_0L\).  The exponential-moment proof of the binomial Chernoff inequalities therefore yields
\[
 Q_P^{(n)}(\mathcal A^c)
 \le 2d\exp(-c\lambda_0L)\le Cn^{-6}
\tag{7}
\]
uniformly for \(d\le\rho_\epsilon nL\), after reducing \(\rho_\epsilon\le1\).  Here and below numerical constants are absolute unless decorated by \(\epsilon\).

Condition on the pilot block and suppose \(\mathcal A\) holds.  The selected light set is then deterministic relative to block \(I_1\) and is contained in \(\{k:p_k\le B/4\}\).  For sufficiently large \(N_\epsilon\),
\[
 K\ge2,\qquad 4(K+2)^2\le m_1,
 \qquad \frac{4(K+2)}{m_1}\le\frac{3B}{4},
\tag{8}
\]
so Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:linear\text{-}mark\text{-}factorial\text{-}covariance}\) applies.  Equations (5)--(6), the variance--bias identity, and that lemma give
\[
 \begin{split}
 E\left[\left\{
 \sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}\widehat P_k
 -\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}\varphi_k
 \right\}^2\middle|I_0\right]
 &\le C_\epsilon\left[\frac1{m_1}
 +6^{2K}\left\{dB^2+\frac{d^2K^2B^2}{m_1}\right\}
 +\frac{d^2B^2}{K^4}\right].
\end{split}
\tag{9}
\]
Put \(\kappa:=2\alpha_0\log6\le1/32\).  Since \(6^{2K}\le n^\kappa\), \(B\le CL/n\), and \(K\le CL\),
\[
 n^\kappa\frac{dL^2}{n^2}
 \le C\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2L^2}\right\},
 \qquad
 n^\kappa\frac{d^2L^4}{n^3}
 \le C\frac{d^2}{n^2L^2}.
\tag{10}
\]
For the first inequality, set \(q=d/(\sqrt nL)\), use \(2q\le1+q^2\), and note that \(n^{\kappa-1/2}L^3\) is bounded.  The second follows because \(n^{\kappa-1}L^6\) is bounded.  Moreover \(dB/K^2\le Cd/(nL)\).  Hence (9)--(10) prove
\[
 E\left[\left\{
 \sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}\widehat P_k
 -\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}\varphi_k
 \right\}^2\middle|I_0\right]
 \le C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2L^2}\right\}
\tag{11}
\]
on \(\mathcal A\).

We now prove the analogous heavy-cell bound, including the missing-arm boundary.  Conditional on the pilot, write \(\mathcal H:=\widehat{\mathcal H}\), which is deterministic for block \(I_1\), and let \(m=m_1\).  Conditional on the category and treatment indicators in this block, (2) gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\left(\sum_{k\in\mathcal H}\widehat h_k
 \middle|(X_i,A_i)_{i\in I_1}\right)
 \le \frac1{m^2}\sum_{k\in\mathcal H}N_k^2
 \left\{\frac{\mathbf1\{N_{1k}>0\}}{N_{1k}}
 +\frac{\mathbf1\{N_{0k}>0\}}{N_{0k}}\right\}.
\tag{12}
\]
Given \(N_k=t\), each arm count is binomial with success probability in \([\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\).  The identity
\[
 E[(D+1)^{-1}]=\frac{1-(1-q)^{t+1}}{(t+1)q},
 \qquad D\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(t,q),
\]
and \(D^{-1}\mathbf1\{D>0\}\le2(D+1)^{-1}\) imply that the expectation of (12) is at most
\[
 \frac{C_\epsilon}{m^2}\sum_{k=1}^dE[N_k]le\frac{C_\epsilon}{m}.
\tag{13}
\]

The conditional outcome mean of the heavy sum equals
\[
 \frac1m\sum_{k\in\mathcal H}N_k(\nu_{1k}-\nu_{0k})
 -R_1+R_0,
 \qquad
 R_a:=\frac1m\sum_{k\in\mathcal H}N_k\nu_{ak}\mathbf1\{N_{ak}=0\}.
\tag{14}
\]
The first term in (14) is the empirical mean of the bounded function
\(\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal H\}(\nu_{1X}-\nu_{0X})\).  It is unbiased for \(\sum_{k\in\mathcal H}\varphi_k\) and has variance at most \(1/m\).

It remains to bound \(R_a\).  Put \(q_{ak}:=P(A=a\mid X=k)\), \(s_{ak}=p_kq_{ak}\), and \(r_{ak}:=p_k(1-q_{ak})\).  Exact multinomial factorial moments give
\[
 \begin{split}
 E[N_k^2\mathbf1\{N_{ak}=0\}]
 &=mr_{ak}(1-s_{ak})^{m-1}
 +m(m-1)r_{ak}^2(1-s_{ak})^{m-2},\\
 E[N_kN_\ell\mathbf1\{N_{ak}=N_{a\ell}=0\}]
 &=m(m-1)r_{ak}r_{a\ell}
 (1-s_{ak}-s_{a\ell})^{m-2},\qquad k\ne\ell.
 \end{split}
\tag{15}
\]
Using \(|\nu_{ak}|\le1/2\), \(s_{ak}\ge\epsilon p_k\), and \(r_{ak}\le p_k\), (15) yields
\[
 E[R_a^2]
 \le C_\epsilon\left[\frac1m+
 \left\{\sum_{k\in\mathcal H}p_k e^{-c_\epsilon mp_k}\right\}^2\right].
\tag{16}
\]
On \(\mathcal A\), every \(k\in\mathcal H\) has \(p_k\ge B_-\ge cL/n\).  Once \(N_\epsilon\) is enlarged, the function \(x\mapsto xe^{-c_\epsilon mx}\) is decreasing on this interval and
\[
 \sup_{x\ge B_-}xe^{-c_\epsilon mx}
 \le \frac{C_\epsilon}{nL}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 E[R_a^2]\le C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2L^2}\right\}.
\tag{17}
\]
Combining (13)--(14) and (17) gives
\[
 E\left[\left\{
 \sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}}\widehat h_k
 -\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}}\varphi_k
 \right\}^2\middle|I_0\right]
 \le C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2L^2}\right\}
\tag{18}
\]
on \(\mathcal A\).

Let \(Z\) denote the normalized, unclipped sum of the heavy and light terms.  The selected sets partition \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\), so (1), (11), (18), and \((u+v)^2\le2u^2+2v^2\) show
\[
 E[\mathbf1_{\mathcal A}\{Z-\tau(P)/M\}^2]
 \le C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2L^2}\right\}.
\tag{19}
\]
Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:scale\text{-}sanity}\) gives \(\tau(P)/M\in[-1,1]\).  Projection onto \([-1,1]\) cannot increase loss on \(\mathcal A\), and its loss is at most four on \(\mathcal A^c\).  Equations (7) and (19), followed by restoration of \(M^2\), prove
\[
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_\epsilon M^2\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2L^2}\right\}
\tag{20}
\]
whenever \(n\ge N_\epsilon\) and \(d\le\rho_\epsilon nL\).  Taking \(\rho_\epsilon\le1\) makes the second term in (20) equal to the required minimum branch in this construction regime.

If \(d>\rho_\epsilon nL\), the prescribed estimator is zero and Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:scale\text{-}sanity}\) gives squared loss at most \(M^2\).  Since
\[
 \min\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n^2L^2}\right\}\ge\rho_\epsilon^2,
\]
this loss is bounded by the asserted right-hand side after enlarging \(C_\epsilon\).  If \(n<N_\epsilon\), the same zero fallback is bounded because \(1\le N_\epsilon/n\).  These arguments cover, in particular, all \(1\le d\le c_\epsilon n^2/L\), after choosing any positive \(c_\epsilon\) no larger than the dimension constant in the statement.

Finally, every displayed empirical arm ratio is explicitly multiplied by its positive-denominator indicator, and the outer clipping is defined on all real inputs.  The factorial statistic can be evaluated after aggregation from the marked cell sum and falling-factorial cell counts; for example its unnormalized ordered sum is
\[
 \left(\sum_{i\in I_1}V_i\mathbf1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\}\right)
 (N_{ak}^{(1)}-1)_j(N_k^{(1)}-j-1),
\]
with value zero when there are insufficient distinct indices.  Computing the Chebyshev coefficients and all degrees therefore takes at most \(O(dK^2)\) arithmetic operations after cell aggregation.  The construction is measurable, clipped into \([-M,M]\), and has the stated bounded fallback at every division boundary.
statements.justification: The explicit estimator closes the unrestricted effective-sample-enlargement upper branch for real outcomes.
statements.gap: The proof supplies the marked factorial covariance and fixed-sample calibration absent from the construction handle.
statements.consumer: The robust upper-construction answer and the selector theorem.

statements.statement:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are constants \(0<c_{\epsilon}\le C_{\epsilon}<\infty\) such that, uniformly over \(0\le\sigma\le2\) and \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/\log(en)\),
\[
 c_{\epsilon}M^2\left\{\frac1n+\frac d{n^2}+\sigma^2\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)\right\}
 \le\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2r_{n,d,\sigma}.
\]
Both inequalities hold on the same real-outcome, arbitrary-cell-mass class.  This is a two-sided minimax bracket, not a claim that the two displayed benchmarks are uniformly order-equivalent at every shrinking interior radius.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).  Let \(c_{U,\epsilon}>0\) be the dimension-range constant in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:frontier\text{-}upper}\), and let \(c_{L,\epsilon}>0\) be the corresponding constant in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:radius\text{-}channel\text{-}converse}\).  Put
\[
 c_{0,\epsilon}:=\min\{c_{U,\epsilon},c_{L,\epsilon},1\}.
\]
For every \(0\le\sigma\le2\) and \(1\le d\le c_{0,\epsilon}n^2/\log(en)\), Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:frontier\text{-}upper}\) gives
\[
 \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \le C_{U,\epsilon}M^2r_{n,d,\sigma}.
\tag{1}
\]
The witness in (1) is the single data-driven total selector from Definition~\(\mathrm{def:total\text{-}estimator}\), so (1) is a minimax upper bound for Definition~\(\mathrm{def:minimax\text{-}risk}\), not a law-dependent oracle bound.  Its divisions have the bounded fallbacks specified in the two component constructions, and clipping keeps its range inside \([-M,M]\).

On the same radius and dimension range, Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:radius\text{-}channel\text{-}converse}\) gives
\[
 \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \ge c'_{L,\epsilon}M^2\left\{
 \frac1n+\frac d{n^2}
 +\sigma^2\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)
 \right\}.
\tag{2}
\]
The \(n^{-1}\) boundary component is also supplied for every \(n,d\ge1\) by Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:parametric\text{-}lower}\).  The other terms in (2) are obtained by restricting the supremum in Definition~\(\mathrm{def:minimax\text{-}risk}\) to subclasses of \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\); hence the lower and upper sides use the same model class.

Choose
\[
 c_{\epsilon}:=\min\{c_{0,\epsilon},c'_{L,\epsilon},C_{U,\epsilon}\},
 \qquad
 C_{\epsilon}:=\max\{C_{U,\epsilon},c_{\epsilon}\}.
\]
After decreasing the common dimension-range constant if necessary, \(0<c_{\epsilon}\le C_{\epsilon}<\infty\), and (1)--(2) give the displayed bracket.

Definition~\(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\) imposes fixed overlap only on positive-mass cells, the conditional-mean envelope, the conditional fourth-central-moment bound, and the radius constraint.  Thus zero-mass cells are immaterial, no rank or density condition is used, and all conditioning and division steps are covered by the stated overlap and fallback conditions.  Equations (1)--(2) establish only the bracket; no comparison of its two benchmarks at shrinking interior radii was used or asserted.
statements.justification: This is the honest all-radius same-class minimax conclusion: a proved bracket whose matched regimes are stated separately.
statements.gap: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy provide the binary endpoint bounds and collision upper branch but leave uniform radius dependence open; the present converse does not close the shrinking-radius triangular regime.
statements.consumer: A downstream reader can use the upper benchmark for estimator choice and the lower benchmark for impossibility claims without treating the remaining logarithmic gap as solved.

statements.statement:
Let \(\mathcal D_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) denote the binary-outcome class with arbitrary cell masses, fixed overlap \(\epsilon\), consistency, conditional exchangeability, and arm means in \([0,1]\), and let \(\mathcal H_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) be its uniform-mass, exactly homogeneous subclass.  The affine map
\[
 \Phi_M:\quad B(a)\longmapsto Y(a):=M\{B(a)-1/2\},\qquad Y=Y(A),
\]
embeds \(\mathcal D_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) into \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\), and embeds \(\mathcal H_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) into \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,0}\subseteq\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) for every \(0\le\sigma\le2\).  The image is a strict subclass of the note's real-outcome class.  Restriction to the image of \(\mathcal H_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) transfers the lower term \(M^2(n^{-1}+d/n^2)\), while applying the hypothesis-independent channel in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:radius\text{-}channel\text{-}converse}\) to the binary one-arm hard family transfers the radius term
\[
 M^2\sigma^2\min\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right\}.
\]
Thus the lower bounds arise by subclass restriction, whereas the explicit signed-mark upper estimator is proved on the broader fourth-moment real-outcome class.
statements.proof_tex:
Take a source law in \(\mathcal D_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\), with binary potential responses \(B(0),B(1)\).  If only the observed conditional Bernoulli laws are specified, augment them by drawing \(B(0),B(1)\) conditional on \(X\), independently of \(A\), with the prescribed arm means.  This augmentation preserves the observed source experiment and makes consistency and conditional exchangeability explicit.  Define
\[
 Y(a):=M\{B(a)-1/2\},\qquad Y:=Y(A).
\tag{1}
\]
Consistency follows from (1), conditional exchangeability follows from the source construction, and the propensity and cell-mass coordinates are unchanged, so fixed overlap is preserved.

If \(\eta_{ak}:=E[B\mid A=a,X=k]\), then
\[
 \mu_{ak}=M(\eta_{ak}-1/2)\in[-M/2,M/2].
\tag{2}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 |Y-\mu_{ak}|=M|B-\eta_{ak}|\le M,
\]
so
\[
 E[(Y-\mu_{ak})^4\mid A=a,X=k]\le M^4.
\tag{3}
\]
Equations (1)--(3) verify every member-property of \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\), including the support and moment boundaries.  Cell effects and the ATE are scaled by \(M\):
\[
 \tau_k=M(\eta_{1k}-\eta_{0k}),
 \qquad
 \tau(P)=M\sum_{k=1}^dp_k(\eta_{1k}-\eta_{0k}).
\tag{4}
\]
Consequently exact homogeneity in \(\mathcal H_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) gives \(\delta_k=0\) on every positive-mass cell.  The uniform masses remain \(p_k=1/d\), and the image lies in \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,0}\), hence in every radius class.

The containment is strict.  Put all mass on \(X=1\), draw \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independently of two independent variables \(Z_0,Z_1\), each uniform on \(\{-M/4,0,M/4\}\), and set \(Y(a)=Z_a\), \(Y=Y(A)\).  The arm means and every cell effect are zero, so the mean and every radius condition hold.  Also
\[
 E[Z_a^4]=M^4/384\le M^4.
\tag{5}
\]
Thus this law is in \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) for every \(\sigma\), but its three-point conditional outcome law is not supported on the two points \(\{-M/2,M/2\}\); it is not in the affine binary image.

On the exact-homogeneity image, \(B=Y/M+1/2\) is invertible and squared ATE error is multiplied by \(M^2\).  Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:scaled\text{-}binary\text{-}exact\text{-}lower\text{-}transfer}\) therefore transfers the \(M^2(n^{-1}+d/n^2)\) lower bound from the uniform-mass subclass.  For the unrestricted one-arm family, Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:radius\text{-}channel\text{-}converse}\) applies a hypothesis-independent Markov kernel, so data processing preserves the source total-variation control and scales its separation to yield
\[
 c_{\epsilon}M^2\sigma^2
 \min\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right\}.
\tag{6}
\]
These are lower transfers by restriction to binary subclasses.  By contrast, Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:continuous\text{-}ratio\text{-}polynomial\text{-}upper}\) proves its signed-mark estimator uniformly over all laws in the fourth-moment real-outcome class, including the three-point witness above.  This distinguishes the proved broader-class construction from a claim that merely allowing real outcomes is itself novel.
statements.justification: This proposition makes the published binary subclasses and every converse transfer explicit while separating them from the broader-class upper theorem.
statements.gap: The anchor anticipates moment-bounded extensions, so real outcomes alone are not positioned as novel; it does not provide this note's fixed-sample signed-mark estimator.
statements.consumer: The proposition audits exactly which lower bounds transfer by subclass restriction and why the upper construction applies beyond those subclasses.

statements.statement:
In the unresolved triangular regime \(\log^2(en)<d<n\log(en)\) with \(\sigma=\sigma_n\to0\), can one either construct a realization-wise radius-constrained paired-cell moment-matching fuzzy experiment in \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) having ATE separation of order
\[
 M\min\left\{\sigma,\frac{d}{n\log(en)}\right\}
\]
and sample-mixture total variation bounded away from one, or construct an explicit total estimator whose risk improves the selector's current remainder?  The existing hypothesis-independent channel gives only the product separation
\[
 M\sigma\min\left\{1,\frac{d}{n\log(en)}\right\},
\]
so reusing that channel does not answer this question.
statements.justification: This isolates the only remaining rate question after the proved fixed-radius and dimension-regime comparisons.
statements.gap: The existing channel contracts the source separation multiplicatively by the radius and therefore cannot yield the required minimum-type separation.
statements.consumer: Either answer would settle the uniform shrinking-radius minimax rate in the exact triangular regime where the current benchmarks separate.

sampling_model.design: Observational sampling under the induced product law \(Q_P^{(n)}=P_O^{\otimes n}\), with the one-unit full-data law \(P\) satisfying consistency and conditional exchangeability.
sampling_model.units: \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\) for \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), independently distributed with common law \(P_O\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment with fixed strong overlap \(\epsilon\le P(A=1\mid X=k)\le1-\epsilon\) on every positive-mass cell.
sampling_model.overlap: The constant \(\epsilon\) is fixed; the cell masses \(p_k\) are arbitrary and unknown.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The propensity, two outcome regressions, and cell masses are unknown; the total selector combines robust heavy-light polynomial and same-cell collision estimators using known \(M\) and \(\sigma\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Equation (12) on page 10 and Theorem 3 on page 11 bound the binary-outcome collision estimator by the maximal heterogeneity term plus \(d/n^2+1/n\).
Theorem 3 gives the exact-homogeneity collision upper rate, and Theorem 4 on page 12 gives the matching lower bound on the uniform-mass subclass \(\mathcal H(\epsilon)\).
Theorem 2 on pages 8--10 gives the unrestricted binary-outcome lower scale \(d^2/[n^2\log^2 n]+1/n\) in its stated range.
The nonsmooth branch evaluates a best polynomial approximation with unbiased factorial-moment estimators, while the smooth branch uses a bias-corrected plug-in estimator.
Best-polynomial upper constructions and moment-matching lower priors are dual tools for large-alphabet minimax estimation.
A multivariate median construction attains sub-Gaussian mean performance under finite second moments.

tldr: High-dimensional discrete adjustment has two information sources: rare-cell polynomial smoothing estimates the unrestricted ATE, while treated-control collisions exploit nearly common cell effects. Under fixed overlap, arbitrary cell masses, real outcomes with conditional means normalized to \([-M/2,M/2]\), a conditional fourth central moment bounded by \(M^4\), and maximal cell-effect deviation at most \(\sigma M\), the target minimax MSE is \(M^2\{n^{-1}+\min[1,d^2/(n^2\log^2(en)),\sigma^2+d/n^2]\}\). The scale normalization makes \(\sigma=2\) exactly unrestricted. The constructive question seeks no-extra-log robust component estimators for an explicit total selector, and the converse question seeks one same-class radius-indexed moment-matching family rather than separate endpoint examples.

project_justification.gap: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy give the unrestricted lower bound in Theorem 2, the approximate-homogeneity upper bound in Theorem 3, and the exact-homogeneity uniform-mass lower bound in Theorem 4; Section 4.2 on page 12 explicitly leaves sharp minimax dependence on the maximal heterogeneity radius open.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a three-branch phase diagram in which collision information controls small radii, the radius itself is the bottleneck in the middle, and large-alphabet polynomial smoothing takes over before heterogeneity is unrestricted.
project_justification.fill: The project defines a total known-radius selector from robust polynomial and collision inputs, derives the exact collision target and corrected scale endpoint, and seeks one same-class radius-indexed converse matching all three branches for continuous outcomes.

related_work: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy study the same discrete observational structure for binary outcomes. Their equation (12) on page 10 and Theorem 3 on page 11 give the approximate-homogeneity collision upper branch; Theorem 2 on pages 8--10 gives the unrestricted lower branch; Theorem 4 and Section 4.2 on page 12 give the exact-homogeneity uniform-mass lower bound and state that sharp radius dependence remains open. Jiao, Venkat, Han, and Weissman provide the heavy-light architecture based on best-polynomial approximation and factorial-moment lifting. Wu and Yang connect polynomial upper constructions to moment-matching lower priors. Hoeffding supplies the order-two projection decomposition relevant to collision statistics. Lugosi and Mendelson motivate weak-moment robust aggregation but do not supply the conditional moment assumptions or the marked factorial construction used here. Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman derive a causal minimax interpolation for smooth heterogeneous-effect estimation, not for a growing discrete alphabet or maximal effect homogeneity.
technical_internal_limitation: The proposal does not claim inference, adaptation to unknown \(M\) or \(\sigma\), sharp constants, or a preferred finite-sample tuning. The mean interval is a normalization that preserves the requested \(\sigma\in[0,2]\) endpoint; replacing it by \(|\mu_{ak}|\le M\) would enlarge the automatically unrestricted radius to four and would change the headline parameterization.
honest_scope: Identification, the collision expectation identity, and the endpoint algebra are settled targets for verification. The open mathematical content is the weak-moment no-extra-log construction and the same-class radius-indexed fuzzy-hypothesis converse. The proof program does not address deteriorating overlap, latent effect groups, inference, or adaptation to unknown scale or radius.
